title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Universal Questions Denial Is Worthless Against Proof

questions.question: What does the passage say will be discussed here instead of giving a full explanation of the whole truth?
questions.answer: It says the discussion will focus on two dangerous sources of doubt that weaken a person’s certainty in faith in this time.

questions.question: How are the ways of safety from the first danger introduced?
questions.answer: They are introduced as two main points or two “matters.”

questions.question: In general issues, what is the basic difference between proving something and denying it?
questions.answer: Proof is strong and has value, while denial is weak and does not carry much weight against clear evidence.

questions.question: In the example about the new moon of Ramadan, whose statement is treated as stronger?
questions.answer: The statement of the two ordinary people who actually saw it is treated as stronger.

questions.question: Why does the denial of many respected people not defeat the testimony of the two witnesses in that example?
questions.answer: Because not seeing something is not the same as proving it is not there.

questions.question: When people affirm something with evidence, how do they relate to each other?
questions.answer: They support one another and their agreement becomes stronger.

questions.question: When people merely deny something, how do they relate to each other?
questions.answer: Each one stays separate, because one person’s denial does not really strengthen another’s.

questions.question: What makes the two people in the moon example stronger together?
questions.answer: One gives the claim and the other points directly to what is there, so their evidence joins together.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is broad, unspecified denial hard to prove?
questions.answer: Because it is not tied to one clearly defined place, so it cannot be established easily.

questions.question: If one person says something exists somewhere in the world, what is enough to support that claim?
questions.answer: A single clear sign can be enough to show it exists.

questions.question: If another person claims that thing does not exist at all, what would he have to do?
questions.answer: He would have to search everywhere completely, including all times and places connected to the claim.

questions.question: Why can deniers not truly strengthen one another?
questions.answer: Because they judge based on their own limits, blindness, or lack of awareness, and those limits differ from person to person.

questions.question: What is the difference between saying “I do not see it” and saying “It does not exist in reality”?
questions.answer: The first only describes a person’s own limited view, while the second makes a huge claim about actual reality.

questions.question: How does the passage describe such a sweeping denial in matters of faith?
questions.answer: It describes it as an enormous falsehood that goes beyond what a person can truthfully know.

questions.question: What principle is stated at the start of the second matter about science and art?
questions.answer: People outside a field cannot speak with final authority in that field, no matter how impressive they are in other areas.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the basic nature of unbelief that fights against Islam?
questions.answer: It describes it as rooted in denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: How is belief described in contrast to unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief is described as knowledge, affirmation, and sound judgement tied to real existence.

questions.question: What is the main goal of this section of the passage?
questions.answer: Its goal is to address two major causes of doubt that disturb certainty in faith.

questions.question: Does this section try to restate all the earlier proofs in detail, or does it narrow the discussion?
questions.answer: It narrows the discussion to four questions and especially two deep dangers.

questions.question: How many parts are given as the way to escape the first danger?
questions.answer: Two parts are given.

questions.question: What central rule is taught in the first part about denial and proof?
questions.answer: A denial is weak when clear proof is present.

questions.question: Why is the Ramadan moon example useful in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that actual witnessing can outweigh the denial of many who simply did not see.

questions.question: What is the weakness in the statement “we did not see it”?
questions.answer: It only tells about the speakers’ own lack of sight, not about reality itself.

questions.question: Why does affirmation naturally gather strength?
questions.answer: Because each person who truly points to the same reality backs up the others.

questions.question: Why does negation not naturally gather the same strength?
questions.answer: Because each denial stands on its own and may come from different personal limits.

questions.question: In the example of one person saying something exists and another denying it, which side has the easier task?
questions.answer: The side affirming it has the easier task.

questions.question: Why is the task harder for the one who denies total existence?
questions.answer: Because he would need complete and exhaustive knowledge to prove total absence.

questions.question: What does the passage say deniers often judge by instead of by reality itself?
questions.answer: They judge by themselves, their own minds, and their own limited sight.

questions.question: What kind of claim is acceptable for a limited person to make: a claim about his own view or a claim about all reality?
questions.answer: A claim about his own limited view is acceptable, but a claim about all reality is not.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when someone makes an absolute denial in matters of belief?
questions.answer: He says something false on a massive scale.

questions.question: In the short summary after the first matter, how are affirmation and negation contrasted?
questions.answer: Affirmation is united and mutually strengthening, while negation is scattered and divided.

questions.question: What does that contrast teach about the large number of those who reject belief?
questions.answer: Their numbers do not make their position strong or decisive.

questions.question: What does the second matter teach about expertise?
questions.answer: It teaches that only people trained and grounded in a field can give decisive judgement in that field.

questions.question: What three words best summarize the essence of unbelief in this passage?
questions.answer: Denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What three ideas are used to summarize belief?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgement.

questions.question: When unbelief takes the form of wrongly accepting a false idea, how is it described?
questions.answer: It is described as mistaken knowledge or an incorrect judgement.

questions.question: What is simpler than that, and therefore more common?
questions.answer: Mere refusal to accept the truth is simpler and easier.

questions.question: What kind of denial can be proven?
questions.answer: A limited denial about one specific place or direction can be proven.

questions.question: What kind of denial cannot be proven?
questions.answer: A denial of broad sacred truths covering all beings, the hereafter, and all ages cannot be proven.

questions.question: Why does the passage not fully re-explain the truth it mentions at the beginning?
questions.answer: Because it says that truth has already been firmly established elsewhere, so this section only deals with two faith-shaking doubts.

questions.question: What image is used for these dangers to faith?
questions.answer: They are described as deep pits or abysses.

questions.question: What is the topic of the first matter?
questions.answer: It is about why denial is weak compared with proof in general matters.

questions.question: What religious example is used to explain that point?
questions.answer: The beginning of Ramadan and the sighting of the new moon.

questions.question: In that example, why do the two witnesses matter so much?
questions.answer: Because they are giving direct evidence based on seeing the moon.

questions.question: Why do even many learned deniers fail to outweigh them?
questions.answer: Because their claim rests only on not having seen it themselves.

questions.question: What happens when several people affirm the same true thing?
questions.answer: Their testimonies come together and increase the force of the claim.

questions.question: Why is denial described as isolated?
questions.answer: Because each person’s denial comes only from his own separate experience or limitation.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of one person saying something exists in the world?
questions.answer: Existence can be shown by one good sign, but total non-existence requires impossible levels of checking.

questions.question: What would someone have to know to prove something never existed anywhere?
questions.answer: He would need complete knowledge of everywhere and every past time connected to it.

questions.question: What mistake do deniers make in the way they judge?
questions.answer: They mistake their own inability to see for proof that there is nothing there.

questions.question: Which statement stays within human limits: “I cannot see it” or “It does not exist at all”?
questions.answer: “I cannot see it” stays within human limits.

questions.question: Why is the larger statement morally serious in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it claims total knowledge that a person does not have, especially in matters of belief.

questions.question: What is the short conclusion after the first matter about the nature of affirmation?
questions.answer: It has one shared result, so each true affirmation supports the others.

questions.question: What is the short conclusion about negation?
questions.answer: It is split into many separate claims because each one depends on the denier’s own viewpoint.

questions.question: How does that help a believer respond to the large numbers of deniers?
questions.answer: It shows that large numbers do not automatically give real strength to denial.

questions.question: What major principle begins the second matter?
questions.answer: Real authority in a subject belongs to those inside that subject, not outsiders.

questions.question: Why is this principle important for questions of faith?
questions.answer: Because spiritual truths should be judged by those who know and experience such matters, not by those cut off from them.

questions.question: Why does that make his denial weak in sacred matters?
questions.answer: Because sacred realities go beyond the reach of material observation alone.

questions.question: Who are presented as the stronger witnesses in these matters?
questions.answer: The many truthful spiritual people who have long worked to uncover the realities of faith.

questions.question: What is the effect of their agreement?
questions.answer: It gives powerful support to the truths of Divine oneness and other sacred realities.

questions.question: What is unbelief said to be at its core when it fights Islam?
questions.answer: At its core, it is denial and ignorance, not solid knowledge.

questions.question: What is belief said to be at its core?
questions.answer: It is true knowledge joined with affirmation and sound judgement.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a form of unbelief that tries to establish a false position positively?
questions.answer: It can be considered a mistaken kind of knowing or an incorrect judgement.

questions.question: What is simpler than that positive false position?
questions.answer: Just refusing to accept the truth.

questions.question: How is simple refusal to accept described?
questions.answer: It is described as pure ignorance without judgement.

questions.question: What specific denial can be supported with proof?
questions.answer: Denying that something is in one exact place or direction can be supported.

questions.question: Why can the denial of universal religious truths not be supported in the same way?
questions.answer: Because it would require unlimited knowledge of all existence, the hereafter, and all times.

questions.question: What does the passage choose to focus on in this section?
questions.answer: It focuses on two major causes of hesitation in faith during this age.

questions.question: How many “matters” are given as the remedy for the first cause?
questions.answer: Two matters are given.

questions.question: What does the first matter teach about the strength of denial?
questions.answer: It teaches that denial is very weak when faced with actual proof.

questions.question: What event connected to Ramadan is used as an example?
questions.answer: The sighting of the new moon at the start of the month.

questions.question: Why is the witness of only two ordinary people accepted over many denials?
questions.answer: Because they have direct proof, while the others only report not seeing it.

questions.question: In the passage, what happens when people affirm a true claim together?
questions.answer: Their statements unite and become stronger together.

questions.question: Why do denials not combine in the same way?
questions.answer: Because each denial remains personal and separate.

questions.question: What principle about denial is mentioned to explain this weakness?
questions.answer: A broad denial without a clearly defined target cannot really be proven.

questions.question: If someone says a thing exists somewhere, what may be enough to establish that?
questions.answer: One clear indication may be enough.

questions.question: If someone says that thing does not exist anywhere at all, what level of search would be required?
questions.answer: A total search of the whole world and even past times would be required.

questions.question: What does this show about claims of total non-existence?
questions.answer: It shows they are extremely hard, and often impossible, to prove.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do deniers often use as the measure of reality?
questions.answer: They use their own inner limits, understanding, and sight.

questions.question: Which statement is acceptable as a personal limit: “I do not see it” or “Reality does not contain it”?
questions.answer: “I do not see it” is acceptable as a personal limit.

questions.question: Why is the second statement unacceptable in broad faith matters?
questions.answer: Because it makes a total claim about reality without the knowledge needed for such a claim.

questions.question: What summary is given after the discussion of affirmation and denial?
questions.answer: Positive claims share one truth and support each other, but denials split into many disconnected forms.

questions.question: What does that mean for the apparent strength of many rejecters of faith?
questions.answer: Their large number does not give them real strength against belief.

questions.question: What conclusion should a reader draw from this contrast?
questions.answer: That faith is an immense blessing and central to a meaningful life.

questions.question: What rule opens the second matter about knowledge and authority?
questions.answer: People outside a field do not have final authority in that field.

questions.question: Why is that rule important when talking about sacred truths?
questions.answer: Because sacred truths should be evaluated by those with spiritual understanding, not by outsiders to that knowledge.

questions.question: Why are their denials considered weak in non-material subjects?
questions.answer: Because those subjects are beyond the narrow range of material observation.

questions.question: Who are the trusted witnesses in matters of Divine unity and sacred truth?
questions.answer: The many truthful spiritual people who reached high levels of certainty.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention their long years of spiritual striving?
questions.answer: To show that their insight was serious, deep, and hard-earned.

questions.question: What is the true inner nature of unbelief that struggles against Islam?
questions.answer: It is basically denial, ignorance, and emptiness.

questions.question: What is the true inner nature of belief?
questions.answer: It is knowledge, affirmation, and a real judgement tied to truth.

questions.question: When unbelief tries to hold a false claim as if it were something positive, how is it classified?
questions.answer: It is classified as wrong knowledge or false judgement.

questions.question: What is simpler than building a false claim?
questions.answer: Simply refusing to accept the truth.

questions.question: How is that refusal described?
questions.answer: It is described as complete ignorance without judgement.

questions.question: What kind of negation lies outside the discussion because it can be proven?
questions.answer: A limited denial tied to one place or one direction.

questions.question: What kind of negation is said to be impossible to prove?
questions.answer: A universal denial of major religious truths about existence, the hereafter, and all ages.

questions.question: At the beginning of the target passage, what is said about the truth already proved elsewhere?
questions.answer: It says that truth has already been established with strong evidence, so this section will only discuss two causes of doubt.

questions.question: How are those causes of doubt described emotionally or spiritually?
questions.answer: They are described as deep dangers that shake firm faith.

questions.question: What are the two parts called that help save a person from the first danger?
questions.answer: They are called two matters.

questions.question: What is the key message of the first matter?
questions.answer: Denial has little value against proof in general questions.

questions.question: Why does the passage use an example from the beginning of Ramadan?
questions.answer: Because it gives a simple, familiar case where direct evidence is stronger than many denials.

questions.question: In that case, what makes the witnesses’ claim powerful?
questions.answer: They actually saw the sign they are reporting.

questions.question: What is missing from the deniers’ side in that example?
questions.answer: They do not have direct proof that the moon is absent.

questions.question: How does affirmation lead to agreement?
questions.answer: People who affirm the same reality reinforce one another and move toward consensus.

questions.question: Why does negation fail to produce the same kind of consensus?
questions.answer: Because each person’s denial is based on his own separate lack of seeing or knowing.

questions.question: What is the difference between showing existence and proving non-existence everywhere?
questions.answer: Showing existence may need only one good sign, but proving total absence needs a complete search.

questions.question: Why is a complete search so difficult in this case?
questions.answer: Because it would require checking the whole world and even all relevant times.

questions.question: What wrong step do deniers take from their own experience?
questions.answer: They turn “I do not know” or “I did not see” into “It is not real.”

questions.question: What kind of statement about one’s own limits is still possible?
questions.answer: A person may say that he himself does not see or know it.

questions.question: Why is an absolute statement about reality condemned in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it goes far beyond what the speaker can truly know and becomes a great falsehood.

questions.question: In the brief summary, what is said about the result of affirmation?
questions.answer: It is one and united, and each instance supports the others.

questions.question: What is said about the result of negation?
questions.answer: It becomes many separate results because each denial comes from a different personal viewpoint.

questions.question: What should believers understand from this about the popularity of unbelief?
questions.answer: Popularity and numbers do not prove unbelief true or strong.

questions.question: What happened to some people under their influence?
questions.answer: They were fooled into doubt and lost the certainty of faith.

questions.question: According to the passage, what meaning should death not be reduced to?
questions.answer: It should not be reduced to permanent annihilation.

questions.question: What is presented as the answer to that darkness?
questions.answer: Faith is presented as a great blessing and the essence of life.

questions.question: What is the main point of the second matter?
questions.answer: People who are outside a branch of knowledge cannot give final judgement in it.

questions.question: How does the passage make this point with a practical example?
questions.answer: It says an engineer’s greatness does not make him a better judge than even a low-level doctor in medicine.

questions.question: Why are material-focused philosophers not accepted as decisive in spiritual questions?
questions.answer: Because their attention is trapped in the physical world and they are far from spiritual realities.

questions.question: What kind of people are accepted as authoritative in sacred matters?
questions.answer: The people of truth who have deep spiritual knowledge and certainty.

questions.question: Why is their agreement especially powerful?
questions.answer: Because many of them reached profound levels of insight and all support the truths of faith.

questions.question: What is unbelief called in its essence when it fights Islamic truth?
questions.answer: It is called denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What is belief called in its essence?
questions.answer: It is called knowledge, being-affirming truth, and judgement.

questions.question: When unbelief takes the form of accepting a false idea, how is it viewed?
questions.answer: It is viewed as a mistaken kind of knowledge or judgement.

questions.question: What form of unbelief is even easier than that?
questions.answer: Refusing to accept and admit the truth.

questions.question: Why is that easier form described as absolute ignorance?
questions.answer: Because it does not even rise to the level of making a real judgement.

questions.question: Which subtype is just ignorance without judgement?
questions.answer: Simple non-acceptance.

questions.question: Which subtype involves heart-level consent and partisanship?
questions.answer: Acceptance of non-existence.

questions.question: What kind of denial can actually be established?
questions.answer: A denial limited to a certain place or direction.

questions.question: What kind of denial cannot be established?
questions.answer: A denial of broad sacred truths involving the whole world, the hereafter, and all periods of time.

questions.question: What does the passage choose to present here instead of a full treatment of the truth already mentioned?
questions.answer: It presents two major causes of doubt that disturb certainty of faith in this age.

questions.question: How is the rescue from the first cause organized?
questions.answer: It is organized into two matters.

questions.question: In the first matter, what is said about denial when it faces evidence?
questions.answer: It is said to be very weak and of little worth.

questions.question: What example from Islamic life is used to explain this?
questions.answer: The example of seeing the Ramadan crescent is used.

questions.question: In that example, why does the testimony of two regular people outweigh many denials?
questions.answer: Because they provide direct witness, while the others only say they did not see it.

questions.question: What happens when multiple people affirm the same fact?
questions.answer: Their affirmations support one another and become stronger together.

questions.question: Why do multiple denials not create the same strength?
questions.answer: Because each denial remains a separate personal claim rather than shared evidence.

questions.question: What idea about broad denial is stated as a known principle?
questions.answer: A general denial without a specific target cannot truly be proven.

questions.question: What is enough to establish that a thing exists?
questions.answer: Even one clear indication can establish it.

questions.question: What would be necessary to establish that a thing never exists or existed?
questions.answer: A complete search through the whole world and through every relevant part of the past would be necessary.

questions.question: What does this reveal about universal denials?
questions.answer: It reveals that they demand impossible or near-impossible knowledge.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do deniers often rely on instead of objective reality?
questions.answer: They rely on their own souls, minds, and limited sight.

questions.question: What statement stays within those limits?
questions.answer: Saying, “I do not see it,” stays within those limits.

questions.question: What statement wrongly goes beyond those limits?
questions.answer: Saying, “It does not exist in reality,” wrongly goes beyond them.

questions.question: How is such a sweeping statement described in questions of belief?
questions.answer: It is described as an enormous lie.

questions.question: What short summary is given after this first discussion?
questions.answer: True affirmations share one result and reinforce each other, while negations become many separate claims.

questions.question: Why does this summary matter for believers living among many deniers?
questions.answer: Because it shows that the number of deniers does not make denial strong.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the denier’s understanding of death?
questions.answer: The denier understands death as final extinction.

questions.question: What effect does that have on daily life?
questions.answer: It covers life with bitterness and grief.

questions.question: What does the passage say this should make us realize about faith?
questions.answer: It should make us realize how precious and life-giving faith is.

questions.question: What rule about authority begins the second matter?
questions.answer: A person outside a discipline cannot speak decisively within that discipline.

questions.question: What example from everyday professions is used to support that rule?
questions.answer: The passage compares a great engineer with even the lowest doctor in medical matters.

questions.question: What kind of philosopher is especially criticized in this section?
questions.answer: A philosopher absorbed in material things and limited to what he can physically observe.

questions.question: Why are such philosophers not reliable guides in spiritual matters?
questions.answer: Because spiritual matters go beyond the physical range they are focused on.

questions.question: Who are set up as the trustworthy witnesses instead?
questions.answer: The many truthful saints and spiritual knowers are set up as trustworthy witnesses.

questions.question: What is the importance of their agreement on Divine unity and sacred matters?
questions.answer: Their agreement gives overwhelming support to the truths of belief.

questions.question: What is said to be the essence of unbelief opposing Islam?
questions.answer: Its essence is denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What is said to be the essence of belief?
questions.answer: Its essence is knowledge, affirmation, and judgement connected to real being.

questions.question: How can a form of unbelief appear to be something positive?
questions.answer: It can appear positive when it wrongly accepts or asserts a false idea.

questions.question: Even then, how is that kind of unbelief classified?
questions.answer: It is classified as mistaken knowledge or faulty judgement.

questions.question: What is the easier and emptier form of unbelief mentioned next?
questions.answer: Mere refusal to accept or admit the truth.

questions.question: Which form is described as easy and judgment-free?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance is described that way.

questions.question: Why is that second form required to support its position?
questions.answer: Because once it becomes a conviction, it turns into a claim that must be defended.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation in the final distinction?
questions.answer: Denying the presence of something in a specific place or direction.

questions.question: Why is that first type not the main issue here?
questions.answer: Because it can actually be proven and is limited in scope.

questions.question: What is the second type of negation in the final distinction?
questions.answer: Denying broad sacred teachings concerning the world, all beings, the hereafter, and the ages.

questions.question: Why can that second type never really be substantiated?
questions.answer: Because proving it would require unlimited knowledge of the whole universe, the hereafter, and all time.
